speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned agitation and jaundice, so I need to narrow down the cause. Have you experienced any abdominal pain, nausea, or recent changes in urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and drug use, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools, and do you have a fever or right upper quadrant pain? I would also like to check for asterixis by having you extend your arms to assess for hepatic encephalopathy.
